[← Back to the lesson: Positional encoding](../positional-encoding.qmd)

## Check your understanding

Formative exercises use this page in the [Transformer collection](../exercises.qmd#transformer).

1. Two sentences contain the same words in a different order. Why are initial embeddings alone not enough to distinguish them?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

The lookup assigns the same initial vector to every occurrence of a token, whatever its position. Without explicit positional information or a structural constraint, content-based attention does not carry the order on its own.

</details>

2. Does RoPE add a position vector to token embeddings?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. RoPE applies position-dependent rotations to the query and key vectors, after projection and before the score dot product. It is a relative mechanism, distinct from absolute encodings added to the input representations.

</details>

3. Does the causal mask replace a positional encoding?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. The causal mask is a visibility constraint: it restricts each position to its prefix, imposing an order on the computation, but it encodes neither absolute positions nor relative offsets. The two mechanisms are distinct and often combined.

</details>

4. The sinusoidal formula can produce a vector for a position never seen during training. Can we conclude that the model will generalize correctly to that length?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. The formula defines a signal for that position, but the model still has to learn how to use it. Generalization also depends on training sequence length, data, architecture, and any context-extension methods.

</details>

You have understood this step if you can explain why order must be taken into account, distinguish absolute encodings from relative mechanisms (of which RoPE is one example), separate positional signals from the causal visibility constraint, and explain why a computable signal does not guarantee extrapolation.
